# Tafsir of Surat al-'Asr

It is Makkan.

They mention that 'Amr ibn al-'As came as a delegate to Musaylima the Liar [may Allah curse him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]. This was after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been sent, and before 'Amr became Muslim. Musaylima said to him: "What has been revealed to your companion during this time?" He said: "A short, eloquent surah has been revealed to him." He asked: "What is it?" He said: "﴿By the time. Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe, do righteous deeds, advise one another to the truth, and advise one another to patience﴾." Musaylima reflected for a moment, then said: "Something like it has been revealed to me too." 'Amr said to him: "What is it?" He said: "O wabr, O wabr! You are only two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is digging and scratching." Then he said: "How do you see it, O 'Amr?" 'Amr said to him: "By Allah, you know that I know that you are lying." [[In the soundness of this story there is room for examination. 'Amr ibn al-'As's conversion to Islam came before Musaylima claimed prophethood. Musaylima the Liar claimed prophethood in the tenth year after the Hijra, and he had come to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his people in the tenth year after the Hijra, as in the Sira of Ibn Hisham (3/74). 'Amr ibn al-'As became Muslim in the eighth year, according to the more correct view, as in al-Isaba by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar (3/2). Then I came across what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar relates in al-Isaba (3/225): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Amr ibn al-'As to Bahrain, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while he was there; that he passed by Musaylima, who gave him safe conduct, and then said to him: "Muhammad was sent with weighty matters and I was sent with trivial ones..." and he mentioned something like the story, attributing it to Ibn Shahin in his book on the Companions. On this basis, what is mentioned here occurred after 'Amr ibn al-'As became Muslim, not before his conversion, and Allah knows best.]]

I have seen Abu Bakr al-Khara'iti transmit with a chain [[In manuscript A: "cited as evidence".]], in his book known as "Masawi' al-Akhlaq" (The Vices of Character), in its second part, something of this or close to it [[I did not find it in the printed edition of Masawi' al-Akhlaq. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned that Ibn Shahin connected this story through the route of al-Layth, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal: "That Qurra ibn Hubayra came to the Messenger of Allah... then he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah sent 'Amr to Bahrain, and he mentioned something like the story." See al-Isaba (3/225).]].

The wabr is a small animal resembling a cat; the largest thing about it is its two ears, and its chest, while the rest of it is ugly. Musaylima wished to compose from this gibberish something with which to oppose the Qur'an, but it did not pass even with an idol-worshipper in that time.

At-Tabarani mentioned, through the route of Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Hisn [Abu Madina], who said: When two men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met, they would not part until one of them had recited to the other "Surat al-'Asr" to its end, and then one of them would greet the other with salam [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (5097), "Majma' al-Bahrayn".]].

Ash-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If people reflected on this surah, it would be sufficient for them."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Al-'Asr is the time in which the movements of the children of Adam occur, of good and evil.

Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: It is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), but the first view is the well-known one.

So Allah, the Exalted, swore by that that mankind is in loss, that is, in ruin and destruction, ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. So He exempted from the genus of mankind, from loss, those who believed with their hearts and did righteous deeds with their limbs, ﴿and advise one another to the truth﴾, which is performing acts of obedience and leaving what is forbidden, ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ in the face of calamities and decrees, and the harm of those who harm them, among those whom they command to do good and forbid from evil.

This is the end of the tafsir of Surat al-'Asr, and to Allah belong praise and favor.
